chapters.title: Deploy with SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA

widgets.title: Sovereign agentic SecOps
widgets.description: SUSE Security finds vulnerable images in a bank's payments platform. An AI agent built with the NeMo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA Nemotron checks the policy and the approved image catalog, and opens one pull request moving them to SUSE images. A person merges, Fleet deploys, SUSE Security rescans.

widgets.title: The architecture
widgets.description: Sovereign Agentic SecOps is a Blueprint in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA. The Studio shows what it is made of.

annotations.text: The architecture of **Sovereign Agentic SecOps**, as the Studio draws it: the agent in its **NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox**, the systems it works with, the shared **NVIDIA** models and the people who decide. Green lines are allowed, red ones refused by the sandbox's policy.
The **agent**: a NeMo Agent Toolkit agent, packaged as one component of the Blueprint. Its sandbox, providers and policy deploy with it.
It reasons with an **NVIDIA NIM** shared by every use case from the *NVIDIA Models (shared)* Blueprint: downloaded once, always up.
Everything else is **outside**: the sandbox refuses it. Enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

widgets.title: The use case at work
widgets.description: The use case's own page, step by step: what the agent does, and what it is not allowed to do.

annotations.text: The use case's own page: the Blueprint is **ready** in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA and the agent's sandbox is up. The OpenShell log on the right shows every request the agent makes.
First: **what SUSE Security sees**.
The agent's sandbox reads SUSE Security's findings through its API, with a key it never sees.
The payments platform's images and their vulnerabilities: the storefront and the payments API carry critical and high CVEs.
Next: **triage**.
NVIDIA Nemotron Embed finds the policy sections that matter; Nemotron 3.5 Lightning turns them into a triage table.
Internet-facing and cardholder-data workloads first, each with its deadline under the bank's policy.
Now **the agent fixes it**.
The agent checks the approved image catalog, files a Gitea issue per workload, and opens **one pull request** moving them to SUSE images.
Its issues and its pull request, waiting for a person.
Can the agent merge its own fix, or switch off scanning?
Let it try.
**403, policy denied**, for the merge and for SUSE Security's settings: enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

annotations.text: The engineer merges: **Create merge commit**.
Back on the use case's page, the step that waited for the merge.
Merged by a person, rolled out by **Fleet**, rescanned by **SUSE Security**: the storefront and the payments API go from critical findings to none.
The change record, and the boundary.
The agent writes the change record for the audit.
And it can't reach the internet: **blocked**, every time, and logged.
